title: Why Tech Stayed Cheap While Groceries Doubled

scenes.narration: Why did TV and audio prices rise only 23% since 2000, while your weekly grocery bill nearly doubled?

visual.text: Why Tech Stayed Cheap While Groceries Doubled

scenes.narration: Official data shows grocery costs skyrocketed by 94% between January 2000 and September 2026.
Over that exact same stretch, TV, video, and audio prices crept up by only 23%.
Silicon manufacturing scales effortlessly with automated factories, but farming cannot escape the rising costs of land, diesel fuel, and human labor.

visual.text: Automation slashes tech manufacturing costs relentlessly

scenes.narration: That is why gadget prices barely budge while dinner keeps getting pricier. The full story is on the channel.
Did your grocery bill really spike by 32% in just a few short years?
Between January 2020 and September 2026, US grocery prices jumped 32%, pacing overall consumer inflation of 30%.
Yet home entertainment electronics stayed remarkably steady, edging up just 17% during the same turbulent period.
Physical harvests depend on unpredictable weather and expensive fertilizer, making food prices notoriously vulnerable to supply shocks.

visual.text: Biological supply chains cannot scale like microchips

scenes.narration: You can delay buying a new television, but you cannot delay dinner. Since 2000, grocery prices climbed 94 percent, while TVs rose just 23 percent.
Did you know that overall US consumer prices jumped 99% since January 2000, literally doubling your living costs?
By September 2026, general consumer prices reached 2.0 times their 2000 baseline, driven by massive shocks like the 9% spike in June 2022.
Meanwhile, TV, video, and audio prices grew by just 23% from January 2000 to September 2026.
High-density microchip engineering and rapid factory automation keep driving consumer tech prices down, even as broad inflation surges.
